description: `[1,2].map(&:to_s)` has *no* block node at all: the desugarer produces `blockpass (sym to_s)`, and Ruby coerces the Symbol to a proc (Symbol#to_proc) at call time. So there is no block node to type and no arrow anywhere in the syntax: a checker needs a Symbol#to_proc rule (sym `s` used as a block over receiver `T` behaves as the arrow of T's `s` method) to manufacture one before the Array#map rule can fire at all.
